beats.intent: ThinkSR preserves a dense carrier while a compact thought process reads and updates it repeatedly before reconstruction.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image field from the compact state that reasons over it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Window partitioning keeps spatial tokens organized for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process runs repeated shared ticks over those windows. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into a super-resolved image. The recurrent tick returns to the thought stage itself, and the same parameters are shared across ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR keeps dense features while compact thought repeats

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features from the low-resolution image, then windowing partitions that field without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The dense carrier is defined before the compact thought process begins. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The window partition produces tokens from that field while keeping the carrier intact.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded, then partitioned into windows

terms.label: encoder maps the low-resolution image to dense features
window partition keeps every token from the feature field

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; its parameter count is the second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison is ordered from the smallest model to the largest. CATANet, RFDN, and IMDN all use fewer parameters than DQ-CTM-SR. DQ-CTM-SR has one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest model in this table.
